text:
maya (arch): quick sync - after last night's canary we observed cascading cold starts when aliases flipped fast. i'm fleshing out a set of metadata heuristics to reduce blast radius without changing tenant pin semantics.
noah (runtime): yes, the immediate unbind behavior today is too eager. idea: introduce a lightweight "softbind" lifecycle so runtime can avoid hard evicts until a signal says it's safe.
elena (infra): curious how this differs from previous "soft" proposals? want to avoid overlap with existing rollouts work.
maya (arch): agreed. differences: 1) explicit lease states surfaced to runtime + control-plane-driven hints, 2) a small set of conservative defaults so older clients see no change, 3) a tenant opt-out path for enterprise. sketch of new rollout metadata: 

rollout_id: rl-20260410-7
mode: softbind       # hard | softbind | sticky
stability_window_ms: 300000  # ignore flips within this window for smoothing
evict_grace_ms: 120000     # defer hard eviction this long after flip
client_probe_hint: prefer-stable
expected_dual_serve: true
tenant_eviction_opt_out: false

noah (runtime): runtime plan: maintain per-alias lease with states: BOUND, PENDING_SOFT_UNBIND, UNBOUND. on flip: mark old BOUND -> PENDING_SOFT_UNBIND, continue serving from cached KV but tag responses as "stale" in traces. after evict_grace_ms and traffic below threshold, promote to UNBOUND.
rachel (sre): telemetry required: alias_flip_count, pending_soft_unbind_seconds, stale_response_ratio, dual_serve_ratio, pin_override_count. need an alert when pending_soft_unbind_seconds > X and error_rate increases.
pete (product): product implications: during softbind window some users may observe mixed outputs. console should show a rollout timeline plus an "expected_dual_serve" badge. defaults should avoid surprising customers.
elena (infra): backwards compatibility: unknown fields must be ignored. default mode=hard. gate softbind with a cluster feature-flag. we'll provide a migration toggle per-cluster.
maya (arch): pin precedence rules: 
- tenant_explicit_pin always wins (highest priority).
- cluster_admin_force_pin overrides tenant pins for emergency (audit logged).
- rollout softbind only applies to non-pinned aliases.
this avoids surprising tenants who intentionally pinned.
noah (runtime): implementation detail: to reduce memory churn, PENDING_SOFT_UNBIND entries should be sharded by last-accessed timestamp and evicted lazily if grace window hasn't elapsed but memory pressure is high. also attach small sampling header to track stale hits.
rachel (sre): please add tracing tag "alias.softbind_state" and propagate span attribute when stale-serving occurs. we want to correlate latency spikes to stale-serve transitions.
pete (product): should there be a customer-facing TTL to opt out of softbind per-tenant? some enterprise customers may require deterministic cutover.
maya (arch): yes, add tenant_eviction_opt_out boolean in metadata; if true, runtime must treat alias_mode as hard for that tenant. require admin auth and audit.
elena (infra): rollout plan: enable softbind FF in staging clusters for 2 weeks, run a flip-storm test (script flips alias 100x over 10m) and assert cold-starts <= 1.2x baseline and error-rate unchanged. then enable on a small canary fleet.
noah (runtime): test plan includes unit tests for lease transitions, integration test for client-resolver behavior, and an e2e where we simulate traffic skew and ensure we don't dual-serve beyond expected_dual_serve tolerance.
maya (arch): open question: do we want a separate "stability_classifier" signal from control-plane that can mark a rollout as "noisy" and extend stability_window dynamically?
pete (product): nice to have for long-running rollouts. but start simple, avoid too many knobs.
rachel (sre): ops-bot, create a ticket for telemetry + alerts and one for the migration playbook.
ops-bot: created TASK-2026-442: "softbind telemetry and alerting" assigned to rachel; created TASK-2026-443: "softbind migration playbook" assigned to elena.
maya (arch): decision: prototype softbind mode with conservative defaults behind FF. owners: noah(runtime impl), elena(infra rollout), pete(product UX), rachel(telemetry/alerts). follow-ups: RFC draft linking schema, console wireframes for expected_dual_serve, and migration checklist.
noah (runtime): i'll post a small protobuf sketch for the alias metadata in the RFC.
maya (arch): thanks all — keeping this thread as the short sync. will link RFC here once draft is up.
